title: Impacts of the 2015-2016 El Nino on the California Current System
query: Using the supplied GLORYS12 daily near-surface temperature and CMEMS biogeochemical reanalysis monthly chlorophyll and nitrate for 1993-2020 off California and Oregon (30-48 N, 130-116 W), test the following findings of Jacox et al. (2016, Geophysical Research Letters, doi:10.1002/2016GL069716): (1) the 2015-2016 El Nino affected the physical state of the California Current System less than expected from its tropical strength, and less than the 1997-1998 El Nino; (2) temperature anomalies in 2015-2016 reflected the persistence of the multiyear warm anomaly that began in 2014 more than El Nino itself; (3) phytoplankton biomass stayed low in spring and summer 2016. Give a verdict for each finding (reproduced, partly reproduced, not reproduced, or not testable with the supplied data) with quantitative evidence, and explain differences from the paper.

paper.title: Impacts of the 2015–2016 El Niño on the California Current System: Early assessment and comparison to past events
